chunks: Yūnus, from Ḥammād, from Nuʿmān al-Rāzī, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: Whoever commits adultery exits from iman, and whoever drinks wine exits from iman, and whoever deliberately breaks the fast for one day of the month of Ramadan exits from iman.

key_terms.الْإِيمَانِ: faith; here, the state of true believing from which one departs through grave sin
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the obligatory month of fasting

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) say about adultery, drinking wine, and deliberately breaking the Ramadan fast?
ai.summary: This hadith warns that certain grave sins are so severe that they are described as causing a person to exit from iman. It emphasizes the moral and spiritual seriousness of adultery, drinking wine, and deliberately breaking a fast in the month of Ramadan.

en.hubeali: Yunus, from Hammad, from Nu’man Al Razy who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The one who commits adultery exits from the Emān, and the one who drinks the wine exits from the Emān, and the one who breaks the Fast for a day from the Month of Ramazan deliberately, exits from the Emān’.
en.sarwar: 5. Yunus has narrated from Hammad from Nu’man al-Razi who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘

Whoever commits fornication suffers the loss of his belief, one who drinks wine suffers the loss of belief and one who breaks intentionally the fast in the month of Ramadhan suffers the loss of his belief.’”
